Hardware - all screws must be adjusted and the bed must not be warped.

docs.title: WeightValue
docs.text:
WeightValue is the value on the load cells in grams. It is displayed in degrees, as it is implemented through the temperature sensor interface. Therefore, Fluidd and Mainsail display degrees.

What is this sensor for?

  • It can be used to measure Z-offset via the g28_tenz plugin
  • You can stop printing if the nozzle hits the part or the part is detached. NOZZLE_CONTROL
  • Without resetting it, the bed mesh will be measured incorrectly.

docs.title: MCU Protocol error
docs.text:
Here are some errors that depend on the MCU:

  • MCU Protocol error
  • Unknown temperature sensor flashforge_loadcell
  • Required MCU command
  • flashforge_loadcell: Required MCU command flashforge_loadcell_h1 is not available

The essence of all these errors is that the Klipper version does not match the MCU version.

You can view the MCU version in the System tab.

For example, you are running Klipper 13, but the MCU used is from Klipper 11 or 12.

Or vice versa. You're running native Klipper, but you've loaded an MCU for Klipper 13.

If your MCU version starts with ?-20230317_182329-ubuntu20-virtual-machine, then you've loaded an MCU for Klipper 12 (AD5X) or Klipper 11 (AD5M/AD5M Pro).

Switch to Native Klipper

Accordingly, Z-Mod needs to load native Klipper.

  • Go to mod_data/variables.cfg and delete the line klipper13 = 1.
  • Save the file
  • Turn the printer off and on (do not reboot!)

If this isn't the case and Klipper is working, run UPDATE_MCU FORCE=13 - this command will install the latest MCU version.

If all else fails and Klipper isn't working:

  • Switch to Native Klipper
  • Install the native Factory firmware, which will install the native MCU.

docs.title: Filament has run out or stopped
docs.text:
Filament runout or jam detected

For AD5M, you need to calibrate the sensor steps by trial and error. Enter this in mod_data/user.cfg

Increase this number. The standard 8 is sufficient for some, but some sensors only work correctly at 17. 

[filament_motion_sensor e0_sensor]
detection_length: 8

Filament jam detected (IFS)

For AD5X, the IFS motion sensor step count must be calibrated manually. Add the following to mod_data/user.cfg:

[zmod_ifs_motion_sensor ifs_motion_sensor]
detection_length: 8

Increase this value—some printers work fine with the default 10, while others require up to 17 for stable IFS operation.

Additionally, filament stoppage in IFS may be caused by:

  • Extruder is loaded with spool 1, but spool 2 is being pulled out — use SET_EXTRUDER_SLOT to sync the extruder’s current slot.
  • New filament is being inserted, while old filament remains inside the extruder.
  • The 4-in-1 modules and their tubes have different lengths, requiring adjustment of filament_unload_into_tube in mod_data/filament.json. Set it to 70 or higher. ➜ More details

The issue may also stem from the inability to unlock the filament in the IFS channel.

Mechanical causes include:

  • Plastic shavings stuck on the pinch roller shaft.
  • Spring disengaged from the IFS channel lever.

Solution: Remove debris, disassemble the mechanism, and reinstall components correctly.

After repairs, test printing and filament lock/unlock behavior using the IFS commands.

docs.title: Before each print, the printer measures the center of the bed.
docs.text:
Before printing, the printer:

  • heats the bed and nozzle.
  • cleans the nozzle.
  • Cools the nozzle
  • Measures the bed center (Starting manual Z probe. Use TESTZ to adjust position)
  • Heats the nozzle
  • Starts printing

This is a feature of the native firmware starting with version:

  • 1.1.8 AD5X
  • 3.2.4 AD5M/AD5M Pro

Solution:

  • Roll back the native firmware to version 1.1.7 for AD5X, 3.2.3 for FF5M/FF5MPro
  • Disable the native display

docs.title: E0120
docs.text:
This is a Klipper error.

Most often it is corrected by the following simple actions:

  • Turn off the power of the printer
  • Wait 10 seconds
  • Power on the printer

To see what exactly is the error:

  • Open Fluidd/Mainsail
  • Go to the console and read the error text
  • Open the Telegram bot @zmod_help_bot and enter the error text or look up the description in the documentation yourself

If you can't fix it, you need to create a ticket.

Native configs

docs.title: Filament
docs.text:
Filament

A macro is a small program written in Klipper/Gcode language.

It can be called from:

  • A GCODE file
  • The Fluidd/Mainsail console (press the English letter C in Fluidd)

Note

The value in parentheses is the default value

docs.title: COLDPULL
docs.text:
Cold pull (nozzle cleaning) without force. Implements this algorithm.

  • Select cleaning material (PETG, ABS, NYLON)
  • Follow instructions in the Fluidd console
  • Remove residue from the nozzle

docs.title: M600
docs.text: Pause and filament change.

docs.title: COLOR
docs.text:
AD5X only

Manage filament type, color, and loading/unloading of spools.

Works only when the native screen is enabled.

docs.title: SET_PAUSE_NEXT_LAYER
docs.text:
Set pause/trigger a macro on the next layer:

  • ENABLE — 0 = disable, 1 = enable (default: 1)
  • MACRO — macro to call (e.g., PAUSE)

docs.title: SET_PAUSE_AT_LAYER
docs.text:
Enable/disable pause at a specific layer number:

  • ENABLE — 0 = disable, 1 = enable (default: 1)
  • MACRO — macro to call (e.g., PAUSE)
  • LAYER — target layer number (default: 0)

Warning

To enable these features, add the following to your start code: 

SET_PRINT_STATS_INFO TOTAL_LAYER=[total_layer_count]

Add this to the layer change code: 

SET_PRINT_STATS_INFO CURRENT_LAYER={layer_num + 1}

docs.title: Start/Stop/Global
docs.text:
Global param

A macro is a small program written in Klipper/Gcode.

It can be called from:

  • A GCODE file
  • The Fluidd/Mainsail console (press the English letter C in Fluidd)

Note

The value in parentheses is the default value

docs.title: LANG
docs.text:
Set the language for Z-Mod operation.

  • LANG - language: en (English), ru (Russian), de (German), fr (French), it (Italian), es (Spanish), zh (Chinese), ja (Japanese), ko (Korean), pt (Portuguese), cs (Czech), tr (Turkish)

Example: 

LANG LANG=en

docs.title: SET_TIMEZONE
docs.text:
Change the timezone.

  • ZONE - time zone (Asia/Yekaterinburg)

More details: SET_TIMEZONE.

docs.title: NOZZLE_CONTROL
docs.text:
Control nozzle collision with the bed or part detachment.

Emergency shutdown of the printer if a weight overload is detected (AD5M and AD5X).

  • WEIGHT - weight in grams (1500)

Settings persist after reboot.

Set NOZZLE_CONTROL WEIGHT=0 to disable this feature.

Control is disabled until the macro is first called.

After the first call, control is enabled automatically during printing.

When using the native screen, macro execution reboots the printer.

Without the native screen, restarts Klipper (configuration files are modified).

Works automatically, but additional macros are available for Gcode:

  • ZCONTROL_ON - enable control
  • ZCONTROL_OFF - disable control
  • ZCONTROL_STATUS - check status
  • ZCONTROL_PAUSE - pause on trigger (only after command queue clears; avoid using on initial layers)
  • ZCONTROL_ABORT - abort Klipper on trigger
  • ZCONTROL_AUTO - On trigger, stop Klipper (if Z height < ZCONTROL_Z) or call PAUSE if z >= ZCONTROL_Z
  • ZCONTROL_Z Z=10 - Set Z height.
  • SAVE_ZMOD_DATA ZCONTROL_Z=10 - Save Z height. If you don't want to enable pause, set SAVE_ZMOD_DATA ZCONTROL_Z=230

To enable nozzle control on initial layers, add ZCONTROL_PAUSE in the slicer at the layer where a pause should be used instead of aborting.

The phrase "Control is not active" means that control is not being used at that moment, but it will be activated automatically during printing.

docs.title: GET_ZMOD_DATA
docs.text:
Retrieve Z-Mod global parameters/flags. After execution, the console displays saved parameters applied at runtime.

Fluidd -> Macros -> Main -> Z-Mod PARAMETERS

docs.title: PLUGINS
docs.text:
Displays the plugin management menu.

In this menu you can enable, disable and completely remove additional plugins.

  • Left column (activation): click to enable or disable the plugin.
    • Green button — the plugin is active.
    • Gray button — the plugin is disabled.
  • Right column (updates): enables or disables automatic updates via Moonraker.
    • UPDATE: ON — updates are enabled.
    • UPDATE: OFF — updates are disabled.

How to completely remove a plugin:

If you no longer need a plugin, make both of its buttons gray (disable the plugin itself and its updates), press SAVE (MOONRAKER RESTART), and then reboot the printer. The system will automatically delete its folder from mod_data/plugins/.

docs.title: GLOBAL
docs.text:
Simplified management of global parameters. Only parameters that can be changed with a button click are available. Parameters that require entering a number, specifying a file name, etc. are not controlled by this macro.

After changing parameters, it is recommended to restart the printer.

docs.title: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA
docs.text:
Save Z-Mod global parameters/flags (applied during every print).

Do not add this macro to start/end Gcode or Gcode files. Call it from the Fluidd/Mainsail console. Parameters are stored in the printer memory in mod_data/variables.cfg and survive a shutdown, so you do not need to enter them every time (do not edit this file manually — you will break Klipper or the mod).

To edit parameters:

  • Go to Fluidd -> Macros -> System -> SAVE Z-Mod PARAMETERS, select the parameter, modify it, and click SEND.
  • Alternatively, enter commands directly in the Fluidd console, e.g., SAVE_ZMOD_DATA CLOSE_DIALOGS=2. Check the output in the Fluidd console.

View saved parameters

docs.title: Print color selection menu parameters
docs.text: Color selection menu parameters are all for the AD5X only.

docs.title: ALLOWED_TOOL_COUNT
docs.text:
Number of tools to show in the color selection menu. This refers to the T0, T1, etc commands in the gcode file, not the physical spools in your IFS.

If Z-Mod is able to successfully scan the file for used tools, this will be overridden and the tools used in the file will be shown.

This setting cannot be used when the native screen is enabled.

See preprocessing

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA ALLOWED_TOOL_COUNT=4

docs.title: SCAN_FILE_COLORS
docs.text:
3MF

For 3MF files, scanning and color mapping are instant; the preprocessor is not needed.

Enables scanning gcode files for which toolchange commands (T0, T1, etc) are used, and what colors and materials they are mapped to in the slicer: 0 (disable), 1 (enable), 2 (disable full scan, but look for data prepared by slicer script)

See preprocessing

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA SCAN_FILE_COLORS=0

docs.title: COLOR_MENU_1_BASED
docs.text:
Determines whether to show 0-based (T0, T1, etc) or 1-based (Color 1, Color 2, etc) labels in the color selection menu. This does not change anything other than how the buttons are labelled and is purely for convenience: 0 (0-based), 1 (1-based)

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA COLOR_MENU_1_BASED=1

docs.title: AUTO_ASSIGN_COLORS
docs.text:
Determines whether to attempt automatic mapping of toolchange commands (T0, T1, etc) to physical filament loaded in your IFS when starting a print. Unless you have enabled silent mode, the color selection menu will still appear; this setting only affects the default selections: 0 (disable), 1 (enable)

This setting will also apply to prints started in silent mode. You can configure it to abort the print if certain errors arise with the auto-assignment: 2 (abort if any materials cannot be matched, allow color mismatches), 30 (abort on any issues)

For custom values for error conditions in silent mode, add the following values together to determine the right setting:

  • 2 (At least one material cannot be matched; eg. the gcode file specifies ABS, but you only have PLA loaded; or material data could not be loaded)
  • 4 (At least one color cannot be matched at all, usually due to file scanning being disabled or failing)
  • 8 (At least one color is potentially a poor match)
  • 16 (At least one physical spool has been assigned to more than one tool index in the file)

See preprocessing

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA AUTO_ASSIGN_COLORS=0

docs.title: PURGE_ALL_EXTRUDERS
docs.text:
Creator 5 / Creator 5 Pro only

Extruder purge at print start:

  • 0 - purge only the first (starting) extruder (default)
  • 1 - purge all used extruders

The extruders purged are those involved in mapping the file's colors to the physical spools. If several colors are assigned to the same spool, that extruder is purged once.

When Auto PA is enabled (PRINT_AUTOPA or the Auto PA button in the print menu), all used extruders are already purged during PA calibration, so this parameter has no effect.

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA PURGE_ALL_EXTRUDERS=1

docs.title: UNUSED_EXTRUDERS_OFF_TIME
docs.text:
Creator 5 / Creator 5 Pro only

Turn off heating of idle extruders during multi-color printing after a set time (in minutes):

  • 0 - do not turn off
  • 5, 10, 20, 40, 60 - after how many idle minutes the extruder heating is turned off

In the menu the parameter is shown as "Turn off idle extruders in N min".

For correct operation, Ooze prevention must be enabled in the slicer (Print settings > Multimaterial > Ooze prevention).

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA UNUSED_EXTRUDERS_OFF_TIME=5

docs.title: MIDI_START
docs.text:
Play MIDI on print start (""), 0 to disable.

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA MIDI_START=Pain-Shut-your-mouth.mid

docs.title: PRECLEAR
docs.text:
Enable nozzle pre-clearing in CLEAR_NOZZLE: 0 (no), 1 (yes) (0).

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA PRECLEAR=0

docs.title: PRINT_LEVELING
docs.text:
Build bed mesh before each print (using native screen if enabled): 0 (no), 1 (yes) (0). For native screen bed leveling, enable "Local Network Only" via the printer menu: Settings -> WiFi icon -> Network Mode.

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA PRINT_LEVELING=1

docs.title: PRINT_AUTOPA
docs.text:
Creator 5 / Creator 5 Pro only

Select PA (Pressure Advance) for each print: 0-no, 1-yes (0).

For Auto PA to work from the native screen, enable "Local Network Only" via the printer menu: Settings -> WiFi icon -> Network Mode.

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA PRINT_AUTOPA=1

docs.title: USE_KAMP
docs.text:
Fast KAMP

KAMP is enabled automatically and works without slow object exclusion. For 3MF the KAMP data is available instantly, for G-code — after the file is scanned.

Use Adaptive Mesh (KAMP) instead of full bed mesh where possible: 0 (no), 1 (yes) (0). Recommended to set SAVE_ZMOD_DATA CLEAR=LINE_PURGE to align purge location with KAMP mesh.

Allows using KAMP when leveling is started from the native screen over the network.

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA USE_KAMP=1

docs.title: MESH_TEST
docs.text:
Test the bed mesh before printing:

  • 0 - No
  • 1 - Test WITHOUT Z-Offset auto-tuning (default)
  • 2 - Test WITHOUT Z-Offset auto-tuning, if the mesh doesn't match, run KAMP
  • 3 - Test WITH Z-Offset auto-tuning, with nozzle cleaning
  • 4 - Test WITH Z-Offset auto-tuning, with nozzle cleaning, if the mesh doesn't match, run KAMP

Z-Offset Auto-Tuning

Algorithm for automatic Z-Offset calibration:

  1. Source data: The printer's memory stores a bed mesh (AD5M/AD5X: 25 points, C5Pro: 100 points) obtained during the last leveling procedure.

  2. Preparation:

    • For AD5M/AD5X the nozzle is heated to the working temperature, wiped on the bed, and cooled down to the bed probing temperature: TEMP_TEST_MAX (151 by default) if the target nozzle temperature is above 230°C, otherwise TEMP_TEST_MIN (121 by default).
    • For Creator 5 / Creator 5 Pro the active extruder is parked.

  3. Measurement point selection:

    • The center point of the mesh is used.

  4. Measurement and comparison:

    • A new probe measurement (PROBE) is performed at the selected point.
    • The obtained value is compared with the value saved in the bed mesh.

  5. Offset correction:

    • If the discrepancy is less than 0.3 mm, the difference is added to the current Z-Offset value.
    • If the discrepancy is greater than or equal to 0.3 mm, the system considers the saved mesh outdated and, if the settings allow, automatically initiates a bed re-leveling procedure (KAMP).

Without Z-Offset Auto-Tuning

Bed mesh validation algorithm:

  1. Measurement: A standard probe measurement (PROBE) is performed at the current point.
  2. Validation: The obtained Z value is checked for consistency with the loaded mesh.
  3. Criterion: The value must be within the range from (mesh minimum - 0.21 mm) to (mesh maximum + 0.21 mm).

  4. Result:

    • Success: The mesh is considered correct, printing continues.
    • Failure: A warning is issued and printing stops or, if settings allow, a bed re-leveling procedure (KAMP) is started automatically.

Notes for the check without auto-tuning:

  • This check is a rough estimate. It is intended to detect critical errors, for example, when a mesh taken for a PEI sheet is loaded for thick glass and vice versa.
  • Do not rely on this check as absolute protection.
  • When using smart cleaning (KAMP), the heating wait occurs near the cleaning location, not in the corner of the bed.
  • The check is performed with a hot nozzle.

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA MESH_TEST=0

docs.title: TEMP_TEST_MIN
docs.text:
Lower nozzle temperature for the bed contact test in MESH_TEST modes 3/4 (with nozzle cleaning). If the target nozzle temperature is 230°C or lower, the nozzle is cooled down to this temperature before probing. Default: 121.

Lower the value if your build plate does not tolerate the default temperature: on PC plates (glass transition point ~145-150°C) and some G10 plates a hot nozzle leaves deep imprints in the surface.

This parameter is not set via SAVE_ZMOD_DATA — enter the command in the Fluidd/Mainsail console (the value is stored in mod_data/variables.cfg):

Example: SAVE_VARIABLE VARIABLE=temp_test_min VALUE=110

  • Recommended range: 100-150. The new value applies from the next print, no restart required.
  • Only used where nozzle wiping/cleaning is performed (MESH_TEST 3/4). In modes 1/2 (default) the mesh is checked at full print temperature without cooling down.

docs.title: TEMP_TEST_MAX
docs.text:
Upper nozzle temperature for the bed contact test in MESH_TEST modes 3/4 (with nozzle cleaning). If the target nozzle temperature is above 230°C, the nozzle is cooled down to this temperature before probing. Default: 151.

Usage is the same as for TEMP_TEST_MIN — lower the value for temperature-sensitive build plates (PC, some G10).

Example: SAVE_VARIABLE VARIABLE=temp_test_max VALUE=140

docs.title: FORCE_MD5
docs.text:
Igor Polunovskiy

Note: Only applies when sending G-code. Not required for 3MF.

Verify file MD5 hash and delete on mismatch: 0 (disable), 1 (enable) (1).

  1. Select and download the file for your architecture and operating system:
  • zmod_preprocess-windows-amd64.exe - Windows
  • zmod_preprocess-linux-amd64 - Linux. Don't forget to run chmod +x zmod_preprocess-linux-amd64
  • zmod_preprocess-darwin-arm64 - macOS Apple Silicon. Don't forget to run chmod +x zmod_preprocess-darwin-arm64
  • zmod_preprocess-darwin-amd64 - macOS Intel. Don't forget to run chmod +x zmod_preprocess-darwin-amd64
  • zmod-preprocess.py - Universal Python. Don't forget to run chmod +x zmod-preprocess.py
  • zmod-preprocess.sh - Linux/MacOS Bash. Don't forget to run chmod +x zmod-preprocess.sh
  1. In Orca, you need to specify: Process Profile -> Other -> Post Processing Scripts.

Here are the options for adding:

  • "C:\path_to_file\zmod_preprocess-windows-amd64.exe";
  • "C:\python_folder\python.exe" "C:\Scripts\zmod-preprocess.py";
  • "/usr/bin/python3" "/home/user/zmod-preprocess.py";
  • "/home/user/zmod-preprocess.py";
  • "/home/user/zmod_preprocess-darwin-amd64";
  • "/home/user/zmod_preprocess-darwin-arm64";
  • "/home/user/zmod_preprocess-linux-amd64";

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA FORCE_MD5=1

docs.title: DISABLE_SKEW
docs.text:
1 (disable SKEW correction), 0 (load skew_profile via SKEW_PROFILE LOAD=skew_profile) (1).

Details

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA DISABLE_SKEW=1

docs.title: LOAD_ZOFFSET
docs.text:
Creator 5 / Creator 5 Pro

On Creator 5 / Creator 5 Pro the Z-offset with the native screen and in screenless mode is the same — they are fully synchronized. If the native screen is disabled, you can change the Z-offset during printing via GuppyScreen, HelixScreen, Fluidd or Mainsail — it will be saved.

Load Z-offset from global parameters saved via SET_GCODE_OFFSET: 1 (yes), 0 (no) (1).

How Z-Offset Works

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA LOAD_ZOFFSET=0

docs.title: DISABLE_PRIMING
docs.text:
Disable nozzle priming via extrusion: 0 (no), 1 (yes) (0).

Details

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA DISABLE_PRIMING=0

docs.title: CLEAR
docs.text:
Select nozzle purge algorithm (LINE_PURGE):

  • _CLEAR1 - Orca-style
  • _CLEAR2 - FF group style
  • _CLEAR3 - FF group alternative
  • _CLEAR4 - Shreider's code (top-right to bottom-right)
  • _CLEAR_TRAP - For brushes (top-right to bottom-right)
  • LINE_PURGE - KAMP purge

If you use KAMP, the purge is forced to LINE_PURGE (instead of _CLEAR1, _CLEAR2, _CLEAR3, _CLEAR4).

If you use LINE_PURGE but have not enabled object labeling in Orca, _CLEAR2 is used instead.

Custom purge macros can be added to mod_data/user.cfg — put the macro name into this parameter.

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA CLEAR=LINE_PURGE

5M/5M Pro: This is not a replacement for the native cleaning (CLEAR_NOZZLE), where the nozzle pokes the middle of the bed and then wipes the plastic off on the bed. This is nozzle priming right before printing.

To disable nozzle priming with a line, use DISABLE_PRIMING

docs.title: MIDI_END
docs.text:
Play MIDI on print end (""), 0 to disable.

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA MIDI_END=Pain-Shut-your-mouth.mid

docs.title: CLOSE_DIALOGS
docs.text:
Automatically close dialogs after print end/cancel: 0 (no), 1 (yes, slow), 2 (yes, fast) (0). For fast closing, enable "Local Network Only" via the printer menu: Settings -> WiFi icon -> Network Mode.

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA CLOSE_DIALOGS=2

docs.title: STOP_MOTOR
docs.text:
Automatically disable motors 25 seconds after print end/cancel: 0 (no), 1 (yes) (1).

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA STOP_MOTOR=1

docs.title: AUTO_REBOOT
docs.text:
Automatically reboot the printer after printing completes (0):

  • 0 - no reboot
  • 1 - reboot the printer via the REBOOT command
  • 2 - without the native screen: reboot the firmware via FIRMWARE_RESTART; with the screen: reboot the printer via the REBOOT command

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA AUTO_REBOOT=0

docs.title: MOTION_SENSOR
docs.text:
Use a filament motion sensor instead of the filament presence sensor (0):

  • 0 - no (the filament presence sensor is used)
  • 1 - yes (the filament motion sensor is used)

When using the filament motion sensor, disable it on the native screen; otherwise, printing will stop.

If the filament presence sensor is used in screenless mode, the following message is shown when it triggers: "Filament has run out. Pause in 30 seconds".

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA MOTION_SENSOR=1

docs.title: SILENT
docs.text:
AD5X only

Do not show the color selection window when starting printing

  • 0 - show the window (default)
  • 1 - do not show the window, use previously set colors
  • 2 - do not show the window, do not use IFS

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA SILENT=0

docs.title: AUTOINSERT
docs.text:
AD5X Only

Automatically Load Filament

  • 0 - Do not automatically load filament
  • 1 - Automatically load filament (default)

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA AUTOINSERT=0

docs.title: ALWAYS_FULL_COLOR_CHANGE
docs.text:
AD5X only

Determines whether or not to skip the color change process if the before and after colors are mapped to the same physical spool.

  • 0 - skip the process (default)
  • 1 - do not skip the process

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA ALWAYS_FULL_COLOR_CHANGE=0

docs.title: USE_TRASH_ON_PRINT
docs.text:
AD5X only

Only when running without the native display

Use trash on color change during printing

  • 0 - no purge in trash chute
  • 1 - purge in trash chute (default)
  • 2 - travel to trash chute after color change but do not purge

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA USE_TRASH_ON_PRINT=0

docs.title: REMOVE_FILAMENT
docs.text:
AD5X only

Only when running without the native display

Unload filament after print completion:

  • 0 — do not unload (default)
  • 1 — unload

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA REMOVE_FILAMENT=1

docs.title: FIX_SCV
docs.text:
Fix incorrect SCV (square_corner_velocity) when rendering acceleration graphs and calculating input shapers.

  • 0 - keep the parameter as in stock (5)
  • 1 - use square_corner_velocity from mod_data/user.cfg or printer.base.cfg

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA FIX_SCV=1

In our printer, square_corner_velocity: 25, but shaper graph calculations and accelerations are based on SCV = 5.

This primarily affects displayed accelerations and calculated smoothing levels. shaper_type_x, shaper_freq_x, shaper_type_y, shaper_freq_y remain unchanged.

However, with correct calculations, the resulting accelerations drop by approximately half.

Recommendation: add the following to mod_data/user.cfg: 

[printer]
square_corner_velocity: 9
This reduces cornering speeds and generally improves print quality with a slight speed trade-off.

docs.title: WIFI
docs.text:
On some firmware versions, Wi-Fi occasionally fails to start.

To fix this, connect to a Wi-Fi network via the native screen.

  1. Call SAVE_ZMOD_DATA WIFI=1
  2. Turn off the printer
  3. Turn on the printer
  • 0 — use Wi-Fi from the native screen
  • 1 — use Wi-Fi through Z-Mod

docs.title: FIX_E0011
docs.text:
Common causes of E0011 error (Timer too close):

  • Host did not respond within the allotted time (0.025 sec)
  • MCU did not respond within the allotted time (0.025 sec)

Specific causes:

  • Frozen Nations MCU mainboard or eboard. Lost communication with MCU 'mcu'. Solution: Reboot. Replace the mainboard (mcu) or extruder board (eboard).
  • Host CPU overload (shaper calculations/graph rendering).
  • EMMC overload (git operations, backups, large file uploads during printing, etc.).
  • Insufficient RAM. Solution: Re-solder the CPU and upgrade to 256MB RAM.
  • Damaged extruder cable. Solution: Replace/fix the cable.
  • Loose extruder board cable connection. Solution: Replace the extruder board.
  • SWAP data loading (SWAP resides on EMMC, which operates at 10 MB/s; SWAP data during shaper calculations can reach 25MB). Solution: Disable SWAP if you have 256MB RAM via SAVE_ZMOD_DATA USE_SWAP=0.
  • MCU firmware crash. Solution: Reflash the MCU via factory reset or use the UPDATE_MCU mod.

Fix E0011 and Communication timeout during homing errors. Changing this parameter will reboot the printer. 0-no, 1-yes (0):

  • 0 - keep the stock parameter (0.025)
  • 1 - set the parameter to 0.1

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA FIX_E0011=1

This error may also occur:

  • Large volume of model exclusions: Solution: Process Profile -> Other -> Output G-code -> uncheck Exclude models.
  • If you disabled swap on FF5M/FF5MPro.

Run the MEM macro and see if there is swap and what size it is.

Enable swap if it is disabled: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA USE_SWAP=1

  • If on FF5M/FF5MPro you run a full test, i.e. PID calibration, bed mesh probing and shaper calibration at the same time.

It is better to carry out all calibrations according to this guide

  • If you use Klipper 13 on AD5X. In this case you can return to the native Klipper by running UPDATE_MCU FORCE=12.
  • If fuzzy skin is used and the CPU cannot keep up with calculating the toolpath. Disable fuzzy skin or tune its parameters.

The Communication timeout during homing error may occur due to high communication latency between the host and MCUs. Round-trip time should consistently stay below 10ms. Temporary latency spikes can cause homing failures.

TRSYNC_TIMEOUT is a Klipper parameter (default: 0.025 sec) that compensates for system delays.

Stock file /opt/klipper/klippy/mcu.py sets TRSYNC_TIMEOUT = 0.025. The patch changes it to TRSYNC_TIMEOUT = 0.1.

How to fix on stock firmware:

  • Format a USB drive as FAT32(MBR).

  • Save the flashforge_init.sh file to the USB:

    • Fix parameter Adventurer5M
    • Restore stock parameter Adventurer5M
    • Fix parameter Adventurer5MPro
    • Restore stock parameter Adventurer5MPro

  • Power off the printer.

  • Insert the USB into the printer.
  • Power on the printer (it will beep loudly).
  • Wait for reboot.
  • Remove the USB.
  • Reprint the problematic file; E0011 should no longer occur.

Manual fix on stock firmware:

  • Install root.
  • Use WinSCP to SSH into the printer.
  • Edit /opt/klipper/klippy/mcu.py.
  • Locate TRSYNC_TIMEOUT = 0.025 and change it to TRSYNC_TIMEOUT = 0.1.
  • Save the file and reboot the printer.

docs.title: FIX_E0017
docs.text:
Fix E0017 error. Changing this parameter will reboot the printer. 0-no, 1-yes (1):

In the stock file /opt/klipper/klippy/toolhead.py, LOOKAHEAD_FLUSH_TIME = 0.5. Original Klipper uses LOOKAHEAD_FLUSH_TIME = 0.250. Our mod works best with LOOKAHEAD_FLUSH_TIME = 0.150.

  • 0 - set to stock value
  • 1 - set to 0.150

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA FIX_E0017=1

How to fix on stock firmware:

  • Format a USB drive as FAT32(MBR).

  • Save the appropriate file to the USB:

    • Adventurer5M-e0017-4.tgz for FlashForge 5M
    • Adventurer5MPro-e0017-4.tgz for FlashForge 5M Pro

  • Power off the printer.

  • Insert the USB into the printer.
  • Power on the printer (it will beep loudly).
  • Wait for reboot.
  • Remove the USB.
  • Reprint the problematic file; E0017 should no longer occur.

Manual fix on stock firmware:

  • Install root.
  • Use WinSCP to SSH into the printer.
  • Edit /opt/klipper/klippy/toolhead.py.
  • Locate LOOKAHEAD_FLUSH_TIME = 0.5 and change it to LOOKAHEAD_FLUSH_TIME = 0.150.
  • Save the file and reboot the printer.

docs.title: LED
docs.text:
LED brightness at startup (50).

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA LED=50

docs.title: WEB_SCREEN
docs.text:
Only Creator 5 / Creator 5 Pro

Redirect the printer screen as a virtual screen camera in Fluidd/Mainsail and zmod.link

  • 0 - Do not redirect
  • 1 - Redirect (default)

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA WEB_SCREEN=1

docs.title: MIDI_ON
docs.text:
Play MIDI at startup (""). Use 0 to disable.

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA MIDI_ON=Pain-Shut-your-mouth.mid

docs.title: NEW_SAVE_CONFIG
docs.text:
Use alternative SAVE_CONFIG (invokes SAVE_CONFIG without freezing the native screen). NEW_SAVE_CONFIG for PID calibration: 0-no, 1-yes (0).

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA NEW_SAVE_CONFIG=0

docs.title: USE_SWAP
docs.text:
Enable SWAP (1):

  • 0 - no (Only for upgraded 256MB RAM)
  • 1 - yes, on EMMC
  • 2 - yes, if possible on USB FLASH(FAT32(MBR)) for the brave and confident (in fact, it works 90% slower than EMMC)

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA USE_SWAP=1

docs.title: CHINA_CLOUD
docs.text:
Enable Chinese cloud services: 0-no, 1-yes (1).

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA CHINA_CLOUD=0

Disable Chinese clouds

Even if all cloud options are disabled via the screen, the printer still attempts to send photos, videos, and telemetry to Chinese servers.

Setting this parameter to 0 partially disables these "features."

If Chinese clouds are disabled, the printer will not check for stock firmware updates.

To update stock firmware, enable Chinese clouds via SAVE_ZMOD_DATA CHINA_CLOUD=1, reboot, and proceed with the update.

Instead, you can use:

  • zmod.link - a cloud for managing printers via Fluidd/Mainsail.
  • Telegram bot.

To disable Chinese clouds on stock firmware:

  • Format a USB drive as FAT32(MBR).
  • Place flashforge_init.sh on the USB.
  • Power off the printer.
  • Insert the USB into the printer.
  • Power on the printer (it will reboot once).
  • Remove the USB.

To enable Chinese clouds on stock firmware:

  • Format a USB drive as FAT32(MBR).
  • Place flashforge_init.sh on the USB.
  • Follow the same steps as above (the printer will reboot once).

docs.title: NICE
docs.text:
Set Klipper process priority: 1 (lowest) to 40 (highest) (20).

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA NICE=20

Higher priority allocates more resources to Klipper but may cause Moonraker and camera disconnections.

For Linux users: 

NICE=20
grep -q "^nice = " /opt/config/mod_data/variables.cfg && NICE=$(grep "^nice = " /opt/config/mod_data/variables.cfg | cut -d "=" -f2| awk '{print $1}')
NICE=$((20-$NICE))
[ $NICE -ge 20 ]  && NICE=19
[ $NICE -lt -20 ] && NICE=-20
renice $NICE $(ps |grep klippy.py| grep -v grep| awk '{print $1}')

docs.title: DISPLAY_OFF_TIMEOUT
docs.text:
Set the time (in seconds) after which the native screen is turned off when working in screenless mode. Default: 180.

Note: The native screen needs at least 5 seconds to configure WiFi.

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA DISPLAY_OFF_TIMEOUT=120

docs.title: PRO_POWEROFF_TIMEOUT
docs.text:
Set the timeout (in minutes) for FF5M Pro to auto-power off. Default: 0 (disabled).

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA PRO_POWEROFF_TIMEOUT=10

docs.title: SAVE_MOONRAKER
docs.text:
• 0 - Load macro button layouts from Z-Mod (default).
  • 1 - Allow saving macro button changes locally in Fluidd/Moonraker.

Locally saved macros are stored in a separate section.

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA SAVE_MOONRAKER=1

docs.title: SAVE_FILAMENT_SENSORS
docs.text:
• 0 - Do not save the state of filament sensors after a reboot; they will always be enabled (default)
  • 1 - Save the state of the sensors after a reboot. If you disable a sensor, it will also be disabled after a reboot.

Example: SAVE_ZMOD_DATA SAVE_FILAMENT_SENSORS=1

docs.title: How to Contact Developer Support
docs.text:
Open the Telegram bot @zmod_help_bot and ask it your question. It knows all the documentation.

  1. Update Z-Mod and all plugins to the latest version via Fluidd -> Settings -> Software Updates
  2. Clearly describe the issue: provide screenshots, photos, and a detailed textual explanation.
  3. Run CLEAR_EMMC to clear previous logs.
  4. Power off the printer completely.
  5. Power the printer back on.
  6. Reproduce the issue.
  7. Run TAR_CONFIG to collect log files.
  8. Submit one post with your description and the generated config-1.6.6-28.tar.gz file, where 1.6.6-28 is the current version of the mod.
  9. Open the issue here.

If it is impossible to execute TAR_CONFIG:

  • Download log
  • Copy config-1.6.6-28.tar.gz from the USB flash drive, where 1.6.6-28 is the current version of the mod

Or connect to the printer via SSH:

AD5M/AD5M Pro:

chroot /data/.mod/.zmod/
/usr/data/zmod/zmod/.shell/tar_config.sh

AD5X/C5/C5Pro:

chroot /usr/data/.mod/.zmod/
/usr/data/zmod/zmod/.shell/tar_config.sh

Create a ticket

docs.title: Why I Ask You to Create Tickets — Explained Simply
docs.text:
Imagine your printer is a car.

And I’m a mechanic in a huge garage, repairing hundreds of different vehicles every day.

You pull in and shout:

“My car won’t drive!”

And I have to start with the most basic question:

“Okay — what make, model, and year is your car?”

docs.title: Why This Matters — A Breakdown
docs.text:
Our “fleet” includes over 100 unique configurations. Just by major categories:

  • 5 different printer models:

FF5M, FF5M Pro, AD5X, C5, C5Pro

  • 3 Klipper “engine” versions:

11, 12, 13

  • 2 CPU architectures:

ARM and MIPS

  • Display options (“interior trim”):

    • Stock screen
    • GuppyScreen
    • HelixScreen
    • Headless (no screen)

  • Primary UIs:

Fluidd and Mainsail

  • Print initiation methods:

Via stock screen, Guppy, OrcaSlicer (using FF protocol, Klipper protocol, etc.)

  • Optional “features” (plugins):

nopoop, recommend, bambufy, g28_tenz, timelapse, notify and others

  • Sensors and peripherals:

filament presence, filament motion, IFS, etc.

On top of that, some users modify hardware themselves, install outdated firmware, or follow advice from forums or AI models that have never seen their specific printer.

docs.title: The Result
docs.text:
When you write just “doesn’t work”, I waste hours just trying to identify:

  • Which model you have

  • Which Klipper/firmware version

  • Whether you’re using a screen (and which one)

  • Which slicer, settings, and plugins are active

That’s inefficient, delays help, and frustrates everyone.

docs.title: ✅ How to “Bring Your Car to the Shop” — Ticket Checklist
docs.text: To help me skip the guessing and start fixing, please follow this checklist:

docs.title: 1. Update to the latest version
docs.text: Follow the official update guide.

docs.title: 2. Describe the issue clearly and concretely
docs.text:
❌ Bad: “It doesn’t work.”

✅ Good:

  • “After updating Z-Mod to v.X.Y.Z, when starting a print from the stock screen:

— the bed heats up,

— the extruder does NOT heat (screen shows 0°C),

— print aborts after ~2 minutes.”_

🔹 Attach screenshots, photos,

🔹 Describe exact steps leading to the issue,

🔹 Attach the G-code file (the problem may be in the file itself!).

docs.title: 3. Run full diagnostics
docs.text:
Do these steps in strict order:

  1. CLEAR_EMMC — clear old logs

  2. Unplug the printer from mains → Wait 10 seconds

  3. Power it back on

  4. Reproduce the issue (start print, press button — trigger the error)

  5. Run TAR_CONFIG — generates config.tar.gz containing all logs

docs.title: 4. Submit the ticket correctly
docs.text:
• Go to Issues page

  • Create one new issue

  • Include:

  • Your clear description (step 2 above)

  • Attach config.tar.gz

  • Attach the G-code file, if applicable

⚠️ Without config.tar.gz, diagnosis is impossible — it’s like submitting a blood test… without the blood.

docs.title: What This Achieves
docs.text:
You stop shouting:

“My car won’t drive!”

And instead deliver:

🚗 Your exact vehicle,

📋 Full service history,

📊 Diagnostic reports.

Then I can start fixing — immediately, not speculating.

Thank you for your understanding and respect for others’ time.

This is not bureaucracy — it’s the only way to make support fast and effective.

Create a ticket

docs.title: Main
docs.text:
Main

A macro is a small program written in Klipper/Gcode language.

It can be called from:

  • A GCODE file
  • The Fluidd/Mainsail console (press the English letter C in Fluidd)

Note

The value in parentheses is the default value

docs.title: START_PRINT
docs.text:
Replaces the default start G-code. For printers with a native screen, add M140/M190 S[bed_temp] and M109/M104 S[nozzle_temp].

Parameters:

  • EXTRUDER_TEMP — extruder temperature (default: 245)
  • BED_TEMP — bed temperature (default: 80)
  • MESH — bed mesh profile name to load (empty = no mesh is loaded; if the profile does not exist, it will be created)
  • FORCE_LEVELING — force bed leveling (default: False)
  • SKIP_LEVELING — skip bed leveling entirely (overrides FORCE_KAMP/FORCE_LEVELING, default: False)

  • FORCE_KAMP — build an adaptive bed mesh (KAMP, default: False). Recommended to add SAVE_ZMOD_DATA CLEAR=LINE_PURGE to use purge areas for KAMP.

  • Z_OFFSET — set Z offset (default: 0.0)

  • INTERNAL - For the PRO version when operating without the native screen, 1 - enable internal recirculation (0)
  • EXTERNAL - For the PRO version when operating without the native screen, 1 - enable external recirculation (0)

Notes:

  • Any calibration (e.g., FORCE_KAMP/FORCE_LEVELING) triggers CLEAR_NOZZLE.
  • ZSSH_RELOAD is called during START_PRINT to restore SSH if needed.

Example for Orca with native screen: Replace the start G-code with: 

START_PRINT EXTRUDER_TEMP=[nozzle_temperature_initial_layer] BED_TEMP=[bed_temperature_initial_layer_single]
M190 S[bed_temperature_initial_layer_single]
M104 S[nozzle_temperature_initial_layer] T{single_extruder_multi_material ? 0 : initial_extruder}

Example for Orca without native screen: 

START_PRINT EXTRUDER_TEMP=[nozzle_temperature_initial_layer] BED_TEMP=[bed_temperature_initial_layer_single]

Layer tracking in Fluidd: Add to start G-code: 

SET_PRINT_STATS_INFO TOTAL_LAYER=[total_layer_count]
Add to layer change G-code: 
SET_PRINT_STATS_INFO CURRENT_LAYER={layer_num + 1}

Bed leveling options

docs.title: Global flags (set via SAVE_ZMOD_DATA):
docs.text:
• PRECLEAR — pre-nozzle cleaning in CLEAR_NOZZLE: 0 = disable, 1 = enable (default: 0).
  • CLEAR — nozzle cleaning method (LINE_PURGE).
  • PRINT_LEVELING — enable bed leveling for every print: 0 = disable, 1 = enable (default: 0).
  • USE_KAMP — use adaptive bed mesh (KAMP) where possible: 0 = disable, 1 = enable (default: 0).
  • DISABLE_PRIMING — disable nozzle priming: 0 = enable, 1 = disable (default: 0).

  • FORCE_MD5 — verify file MD5 hashes and delete the file on mismatch (default: 1). > Note: Only applies when sending G-code. Not required for 3MF.

    1. Select and download the file for your architecture and operating system:
    • zmod_preprocess-windows-amd64.exe - Windows
    • zmod_preprocess-linux-amd64 - Linux. Don't forget to run chmod +x zmod_preprocess-linux-amd64
    • zmod_preprocess-darwin-arm64 - macOS Apple Silicon. Don't forget to run chmod +x zmod_preprocess-darwin-arm64
    • zmod_preprocess-darwin-amd64 - macOS Intel. Don't forget to run chmod +x zmod_preprocess-darwin-amd64
    • zmod-preprocess.py - Universal Python. Don't forget to run chmod +x zmod-preprocess.py
    • zmod-preprocess.sh - Linux/MacOS Bash. Don't forget to run chmod +x zmod-preprocess.sh
    1. In Orca, you need to specify: Process Profile -> Other -> Post Processing Scripts.

    Here are the options for adding:

    • "C:\path_to_file\zmod_preprocess-windows-amd64.exe";
    • "C:\python_folder\python.exe" "C:\Scripts\zmod-preprocess.py";
    • "/usr/bin/python3" "/home/user/zmod-preprocess.py";
    • "/home/user/zmod-preprocess.py";
    • "/home/user/zmod_preprocess-darwin-amd64";
    • "/home/user/zmod_preprocess-darwin-arm64";
    • "/home/user/zmod_preprocess-linux-amd64";

  • DISABLE_SKEW — disable skew correction: 1 = disable, 0 = load skew_profile (calls SKEW_PROFILE LOAD=skew_profile) (default: 1).

  • AUTO_REBOOT — auto-reboot after print: 0 = disable, 1 = enable, 2 = FIRMWARE_RESTART (screenless mode only; with the native screen — REBOOT) (default: 0).
  • CLOSE_DIALOGS — auto-close dialogs: 0 = disable, 1 = slow, 2 = fast (requires enabling "Local Network Only" on the printer screen: Settings → WiFi icon → Network Mode) (default: 0).
  • STOP_MOTOR — disable motors 25 seconds after print end/cancel: 0 = disable, 1 = enable (default: 1).
  • MIDI_START — MIDI file to play on print start (e.g., "start.mid").
  • MIDI_END — MIDI file to play on print end.

docs.title: Bed leveling logic:
docs.text:
1. Load mesh from MESH if specified.
  2. Skip leveling if SKIP_LEVELING = True.
  3. Build KAMP mesh if FORCE_KAMP = True.
  4. Otherwise, build a full mesh if no mesh is loaded (the native screen always loads MESH_DATA) or FORCE_LEVELING = True. The mesh itself is not saved.

docs.title: END_PRINT
docs.text: Replaces the default end G-code.

docs.title: Global flags (set via SAVE_ZMOD_DATA):
docs.text:
• AUTO_REBOOT — auto-reboot after print (same as above).
  • CLOSE_DIALOGS — auto-close dialogs (same as above).
  • STOP_MOTOR — disable motors after print (same as above).
  • MIDI_END — MIDI file to play on print end.

docs.title: _USER_PREPARE_PRINT
docs.text:
Custom macro that is called before the file is sent to print.

Lets you insert your own macros and commands before the file starts printing, i.e. even before START_PRINT runs.

Example override in mod_data/user.cfg: 

[gcode_macro _USER_PREPARE_PRINT]
gcode:
    # Your macros and commands
    RESPOND MSG="Preparing to print"

Note: By default, this macro is empty and can be overridden by the user according to their needs.

docs.title: _USER_START_PRINT
docs.text:
Custom macro for user-defined actions at the start of printing.

This macro is automatically called at the end of the START_PRINT macro. Use it to extend the standard print initialization process with custom commands.

Common use cases:

  • Add custom heating or calibration commands
  • Perform additional setup before printing starts
  • Enable/disable devices (fans, sensors, etc.)
  • Add custom nozzle cleaning or other preparation

Example override in mod_data/user.cfg: 

[gcode_macro _USER_START_PRINT]
gcode:
    # Enable additional fan
    SET_PIN PIN=my_fan VALUE=1
    # Some custom command
    G4 P1000  ; pause for 1 second
    # Other custom actions

Note: By default, this macro is empty and can be overridden by the user according to their needs.

docs.title: _USER_END_PRINT
docs.text:
Custom macro for user-defined actions at the end of printing.

This macro is automatically called at the end of the END_PRINT macro. Use it to extend the standard print completion process with custom commands.

Common use cases:

  • Perform additional actions after printing completes
  • Disable additional devices
  • Save statistics or logs
  • Run custom cleaning or maintenance routines

Example override in mod_data/user.cfg: 

[gcode_macro _USER_END_PRINT]
gcode:
    # Disable additional fan
    SET_PIN PIN=my_fan VALUE=0
    # Send notification
    M118 Print completed!
    # Or other custom commands

Note: By default, this macro is empty and can be overridden by the user according to their needs.

docs.title: CANCEL
docs.text: Cancel the current print.

docs.title: CLEAR_NOZZLE
docs.text:
Nozzle cleaning (as in stock firmware). Parameters:

  • EXTRUDER_TEMP — extruder temperature (default: 230)
  • BED_TEMP — bed temperature (default: 80)

PRECLEAR is not a CLEAR_NOZZLE parameter but a global flag set via SAVE_ZMOD_DATA PRECLEAR=1; it enables pre-cleaning. Learn more.

Overriding the CLEAR_NOZZLE macro in mod_data/user.cfg does not change the native nozzle cleaning when it is started directly from the native screen: the native screen works without Z-Mod and therefore does not use Z-Mod macros.

docs.title: LED_ON
docs.text: Turn on LED lighting.

docs.title: LED_OFF
docs.text: Turn off LED lighting.

docs.title: LED
docs.text:
Set LED brightness.

  • S — brightness percentage (default: 50).

docs.title: PAUSE
docs.text: Pause the print.

docs.title: RESUME
docs.text: Resume the print after pausing.

docs.title: PLAY_MIDI
docs.text:
Play a MIDI file.

  • FILE — filename (default: For_Elise.mid). Files are stored in mod_data/midi/.

docs.title: REBOOT
docs.text: Reboot the printer.

docs.title: CLOSE_DIALOGS
docs.text:
Close dialogs on the native screen (slow method). Used to close the window at the end of a print or when a print is cancelled. May cause printer freezes.

Implementation: @darksimpson

Controlled by the CLOSE_DIALOGS global parameter.

docs.title: FAST_CLOSE_DIALOGS
docs.text:
Close dialogs quickly (recommended). Used to close the window at the end of a print or when a print is cancelled. Works faster and does not freeze the printer.

Implementation: @darksimpson

Enable "Local Network Only" in printer settings: Settings → WiFi icon → Network Mode → Toggle "Local Network Only". Controlled by the CLOSE_DIALOGS global parameter.

docs.title: NEW_SAVE_CONFIG
docs.text:
Trigger SAVE_CONFIG without freezing the native screen. Can be used to restart Klipper without freezing the native screen.

Implementation: @darksimpson

May take ~1 minute and occasionally cause screen glitches.

docs.title: SHUTDOWN
docs.text: Power off the printer.

docs.title: Native firmware
docs.text: Here is the native firmware for AD5M, AD5M Pro, AD5X printers

docs.title: How to install native firmware
docs.text:
1. Before installing, it is best to reset the printer to default settings, if possible.
  2. Format a USB drive (a regular flash drive) to FAT32 or FAT/FAT16 (MBR).
  3. Copy the file to the root of the USB drive (no subfolders).
  4. Power off the printer.
  5. Insert the USB drive into the printer.
  6. Power on the printer.
  7. Wait until it has fully booted.
  8. Power the printer off and on.
  9. Perform the necessary calibrations.

docs.title: Unbricker
docs.text:
Universal unbricker for AD5M / AD5M Pro / AD5X / Creator 5 / Creator 5 Pro

  1. Download the Universal.zip file
  2. Format the USB drive to FAT32
  3. Extract Universal.zip to the root of the USB drive
  4. Turn off the printer
  5. Insert the USB drive into the printer
  6. Wait for the firmware to flash (up to 40 minutes)
  7. Remove the USB drive from the printer
  8. Turn the printer off and on

If something went wrong, check the log files on the USB drive.

docs.title: Installing Full Firmware on Creator 5 / Creator 5 Pro
docs.text:
This is NOT the original Factory firmware, but a printer unbricking tool. It should only be installed if the printer does not start at all.

Installation takes a long time, up to an hour.

  1. Copy all 3 files at once to a FAT32-formatted USB flash drive:
  • Creator5-factory-1.9.7.tgz
  • Creator5Pro-factory-1.9.7.tgz
  • Creator5Pro-factory.tar.xz

  1. Power off the printer, insert the flash drive, power it on and wait for a full reboot. A Creator 5 will become a Creator 5 Pro — this is normal.

  2. After updating, if you need to reflash the MCU, install:

  • Creator5
  • Creator5Pro
  1. To turn a Creator 5 back from Creator 5 Pro into the regular version:
  • Creator5Pro-to_c5.tgz

docs.title: Plugins in Z-Mod
docs.text:
Any user can create and connect their own plugin to zmod.

Plugins included with Z-Mod:

  1. Recommend - Settings recommended for immediate use after installing the mod.
  2. G28_tenz – Z-axis parking using load cells
  3. Nopoop - Maximum waste reduction by ninjamida
  4. TimeLapse - Moonraker Timelapse
  5. Notify - Receive notifications in Telegram and more than 100 other services

External plugins not developed by the Z-Mod author.

  1. Bambufy - Compatible with Bambu Studio, improves feed tower control, provides accurate time and material consumption estimates, reduces waste, supports Mainsail, quick color changes, and advanced printing features. CANNOT BE USED WITH THE NATIVE SCREEN.
  2. lessWaste - a fork of Bambufy
  3. Dryer - Drying filament via heated bed
  4. IFS Jacker - Plugin to support the IFS Jacker hardware mod, for auto-detection of available channel count and Klipper integration for fans / LEDs / sensors connected via an IFS Jacker
  5. HelixScreen - an alternative screen implementation
  6. QuickSwap - Plugin for faster color changing on AD5X
  7. Flook32 - Plugin for connecting the Flook32 dryer En
  8. Print Handy - Reports other AD5X IFS slots with the same color and material. It does not switch filament.
  9. Zmod AFC Lite - Shows the AD5X IFS slots or the Creator 5 toolheads as AFC lanes in the Mainsail and Fluidd AFC panels, with load/unload, color, material and Spoolman spool controls.

To enable the repository of external plugins, run the command PLUGINS.

docs.title: Plugin Management
docs.text:
Enable plugin: 

ENABLE_PLUGIN name=g28_tenz
— downloads the plugin and restarts Klipper on success.

Disable plugin: 

DISABLE_PLUGIN name=g28_tenz

docs.title: PLUGINS
docs.text:
Displays the plugin management menu.

In this menu you can enable, disable and completely remove additional plugins.

  • Left column (activation): click to enable or disable the plugin.
    • Green button — the plugin is active.
    • Gray button — the plugin is disabled.
  • Right column (updates): enables or disables automatic updates via Moonraker.
    • UPDATE: ON — updates are enabled.
    • UPDATE: OFF — updates are disabled.

How to completely remove a plugin:

If you no longer need a plugin, make both of its buttons gray (disable the plugin itself and its updates), press SAVE (MOONRAKER RESTART), and then reboot the printer. The system will automatically delete its folder from mod_data/plugins/.

docs.title: Installing Classic Klipper Plugins with Python Modules
docs.text: For classic Klipper plugins that work with Python modules (e.g., klipper-led_effect), a special installation process is required that involves creating a symbolic link to the Klipper module.

docs.title: Example: Installing led_effect
docs.text:
led_effect is a plugin for controlling WS2812 RGB LED strips through Klipper.

Step 1: Clone the repository

Run these commands in the chroot environment:

# For AD5M:
chroot /data/.mod/.zmod/
# For AD5X:
chroot /usr/data/.mod/.zmod/

# Same for all models:
cd /opt/config/mod_data/plugins/
git clone https://github.com/julianschill/klipper-led_effect.git

Step 2: Add an entry to the Moonraker config

In the file mod_data/user.moonraker.conf, add the following section:

[update_manager led_effect]
type: git_repo
channel: stable
path: /opt/config/mod_data/plugins/klipper-led_effect
origin: https://github.com/julianschill/klipper-led_effect.git
is_system_service: False
primary_branch: master

Step 3: Create a symbolic link to the Klipper module

Create a symbolic link to connect the module to Klipper:

exit
# Native Klipper
ln -s /opt/config/mod_data/plugins/klipper-led_effect/src/led_effect.py /usr/prog/klipper/klippy/extras/led_effect.py
# Klipper 13
ln -s /opt/config/mod_data/plugins/klipper-led_effect/src/led_effect.py /usr/data/zmod/klipper/klippy/extras/led_effect.py

Replace:

  • klipper-led_effect with your plugin's folder name
  • led_effect.py with the module name (may differ depending on the plugin)

Step 4: Restart Klipper

After creating the symbolic link, you need to restart Klipper using the restart button in the Fluidd/Mainsail web interface.

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text: The module must be compatible with your Klipper version Ensure that the plugin version is compatible with your installed Klipper version.

docs.title: Creating Your Own Plugin
docs.text: Plugin example: https://github.com/ghzserg/g28_tenz (In all examples below, the name g28_tenz is used — replace it with your plugin’s name.)

docs.title: Adding a Plugin
docs.text:
In the file mod_data/user.moonraker.conf add the following section:

[update_manager g28_tenz]
type: git_repo
channel: dev
path: /root/printer_data/config/mod_data/plugins/g28_tenz
origin: https://github.com/ghzserg/g28_tenz.git
is_system_service: False
primary_branch: main
  • Plugin path: /root/printer_data/config/mod_data/plugins/g28_tenz
  • Source: https://github.com/ghzserg/g28_tenz.git

Stable plugins may be included in the zmod distribution, but are updated and maintained by their respective authors.

docs.title: Installation Script
docs.text:
After calling ENABLE_PLUGIN, the file install.sh will be executed automatically.

After calling DISABLE_PLUGIN, the file uninstall.sh will be executed automatically.

docs.title: Update Script
docs.text: When the Update Manager updates the plugin, update.sh will be executed automatically if it exists.

docs.title: Single-language Plugin
docs.text:
Must contain the file: 

g28_tenz.cfg
All functionality goes inside this file.

docs.title: Multi-language Plugin
docs.text:
Files are placed in language-specific subdirectories: 

en/g28_tenz.cfg
ru/g28_tenz.cfg
de/g28_tenz.cfg
...

All output strings must be escaped, for example: 

RESPOND PREFIX="info" MSG="===Cutting the filament==="

docs.title: Translation
docs.text:
Translations are stored in the translate/ directory in files like de.csv:

Cutting the filament;Schneiden des Filaments

Format: 

English phrase;Translation in target language

To generate language files, run: 

./Make.sh
The script will create the required directories and .cfg files.

docs.title: Recommendations to Improve Printer Stability
docs.text: These recommendations apply to both stock firmware and Z-Mod.

docs.title: Enable Object Exclusion
docs.text:
Enable object exclusion in Orca:

  • Process Profile -> Other -> Custom G-code -> Check Exclude objects
  • Process Profile -> Other -> Custom G-code -> Check Label objects

docs.title: Install the Latest Stock Firmware and Z-Mod Updates
docs.text:
Only the latest version of Z-Mod is actively supported.

The developer lacks resources to maintain older versions, so install the latest stock firmware and Z-Mod updates.

docs.title: Replace Spiral/Auto Z-Hop
docs.text:
The printer does not support this feature.

In Orca: Printer Profile -> Extruder 1 -> Z Hop Type -> Set to Normal or Slanted.

docs.title: Disable "Arc Move" Approximation
docs.text:
While the printer supports arc moves, they reduce print quality and may cause errors.

In Orca: Process Profile -> Quality -> Precision -> Uncheck Arc Move Approximation.

docs.title: Disable the Built-in Camera on the Printer Screen
docs.text:
The built-in camera consumes excessive memory and offers poor image quality. Use an alternative camera instead.

On the printer screen: Settings -> Camera Tab -> Disable Camera and Video toggles.

Then, run the CAMERA_ON macro.

  • What is an alternative camera?
  • I installed Z-Mod, and my camera disappeared! It worked in Orca-FF!

docs.title: Lan mode error
docs.text:
These services are unstable and may disconnect intermittently. Reconnection attempts can overload the printer with queued requests, causing errors.

Disabling them also enables faster dialog closure after printing and native bed leveling via the screen.

On the printer screen:

  1. Settings -> WiFi Tab -> Network Mode -> Enable Local Network Only.
  2. Settings -> Cloud Tab -> Disable FlashCloud and Polar3d.

Instead, you can use:

  • zmod.link - a cloud for managing printers via Fluidd/Mainsail.
  • Telegram bot.

More about Chinese cloud services.

docs.title: Enable [MD5] Checksum Control
docs.text:
Igor Polunovskiy

Note: Only applies when sending G-code. Not required for 3MF.

Add CHECK_MD5 to your workflow.

It is recommended to use the global parameter FORCE_MD5 SAVE_ZMOD_DATA FORCE_MD5=1

  1. Select and download the file for your architecture and operating system:
  • zmod_preprocess-windows-amd64.exe - Windows
  • zmod_preprocess-linux-amd64 - Linux. Don't forget to run chmod +x zmod_preprocess-linux-amd64
  • zmod_preprocess-darwin-arm64 - macOS Apple Silicon. Don't forget to run chmod +x zmod_preprocess-darwin-arm64
  • zmod_preprocess-darwin-amd64 - macOS Intel. Don't forget to run chmod +x zmod_preprocess-darwin-amd64
  • zmod-preprocess.py - Universal Python. Don't forget to run chmod +x zmod-preprocess.py
  • zmod-preprocess.sh - Linux/MacOS Bash. Don't forget to run chmod +x zmod-preprocess.sh
  1. In Orca, you need to specify: Process Profile -> Other -> Post Processing Scripts.

If the path contains spaces, enclose the full path in quotes — but it is better to avoid spaces in folder names.

Here are the options for adding:

  • "C:\path_to_file\zmod_preprocess-windows-amd64.exe";
  • "C:\python_folder\python.exe" "C:\Scripts\zmod-preprocess.py";
  • "/usr/bin/python3" "/home/user/zmod-preprocess.py";
  • "/home/user/zmod-preprocess.py";
  • "/home/user/zmod_preprocess-darwin-amd64";
  • "/home/user/zmod_preprocess-darwin-arm64";
  • "/home/user/zmod_preprocess-linux-amd64";

docs.title: Send Files via "Octo/Klipper" for Printing
docs.text:
The native FF protocol occasionally transfers corrupted files and lacks metadata support for the Telegram bot.

In Orca:

  1. Click the WiFi icon next to the printer.
  2. Set:
  • Host Type: Octo/Klipper
  • Printer Agent: Moonraker

For Creator 5 / Creator 5 Pro / AD5X:

  • Hostname: IP_printer

For FF5M / FF5M Pro:

  • Hostname: IP_printer:7125
  • Device UI: IP_printer or IP_printer:80

If using Mainsail, specify only these thumbnail sizes: 140x110/PNG, 64x64/PNG

In Orca, Printer Profile -> General Information -> Advanced -> G-Code Thumbnails

Note that the native screen will no longer display thumbnails.

docs.title: Verify Stock OS File Integrity
docs.text:
Improper printer shutdowns can corrupt the filesystem, leading to minor or major bugs.

The CHECK_SYSTEM macro checks file MD5 hashes and repairs symbolic links if needed.

docs.title: Enable Nozzle Collision Detection
docs.text:
Disabled by default. Enable using the NOZZLE_CONTROL macro:

NOZZLE_CONTROL WEIGHT=1500

Once enabled, it activates automatically during printing.

This halts Klipper if the nozzle scratches the bed or a part detaches. Highly recommended for users employing nozzle pre-cleaning routines.

docs.title: Restoring Printer to Factory Settings (Required for Mod Installation)
docs.text:
1. Uninstall KlipperMod if previously installed.
  2. Reset the printer to default settings.
  3. Format a USB drive to FAT/FAT16/FAT32(MBR).

  4. Copy the appropriate file from the Native firmware to the USB root directory:

    • Adventurer5M-3.1.9-2.2.3-20250807-Factory.tgz for FF5M
    • Adventurer5MPro-3.1.3-2.2.3-20250107-Factory.tgz for FF5M Pro
    • AD5X-1.1.7-1.1.0-3.0.6-20250912-Factory.tgz for AD5X
    • Creator5-1.9.9-1.3.0-20260907.tgz for Creator 5
    • Creator5Pro-1.9.9-1.3.0-20260907.tgz for Creator 5 Pro

    Important: Do not unpack the files!

  5. Power off the printer.

  6. Insert the USB drive into the printer.
  7. Power on the printer.
  8. Wait for the stock firmware installation to complete. If it takes too long or does not install at all, use a different flash drive.
  9. Configure Wi-Fi or LAN new beaver
  10. Perform the initial calibrations.
  11. Get the latest printer updates or install firmware 1.1.7 for AD5X, or 3.2.3 for AD5M/AD5M Pro if you don't want the printer to measure the bed center before each print

docs.title: Installing the Mod
docs.text:
Video

  1. Restore the printer to factory settings. AD5X Warning
  2. Format a USB drive to FAT/FAT16/FAT32(MBR).

  3. Copy the mod file to the USB root directory:

    • For FF5M: Adventurer5M-zmod-*.tgz
    • For FF5M Pro: Adventurer5MPro-zmod-*.tgz
    • For AD5X: AD5X-zmod-*.tgz
    • For Creator 5: Creator5-zmod-*.tgz
    • For Creator 5 Pro: Creator5Pro-zmod-*.tgz

    Even better: put all 5 files on the flash drive — the printer will pick the right one itself.

    Important: Do not unpack the files!

  4. Power off the printer.

  5. Insert the USB drive.
  6. Power on the printer.
  7. Wait for the mod installation to complete.

Installation on the AD5X/Creator 5/Creator 5 Pro can take up to 40 minutes. If it takes too long or does not install at all, use a different flash drive.

If you missed the window with the green check mark and the printer rebooted automatically, the standard printer screen will load; in this case you can go straight to step 11.

  1. Remove the USB drive.
  2. Power off the printer.
  3. Power on the printer.

  4. Open the printer's IP address in the browser

    If the web interface doesn't open, the stock firmware has disabled the mod. To enable it, copy the file:

    • AD5X-enable-zmod.tgz
    • Creator5-enable-zmod.tgz
    • Creator5Pro-enable-zmod.tgz

  5. Translate the mod into your language.

    Or type in the console: LANG LANG=en

    Set your timezone: SET_TIMEZONE ZONE=Europe/London (run SET_TIMEZONE without parameters to list zones). Details

  6. Configure the mod

    This shows parameters used at print start, print end, and global settings. It is recommended to just review the settings — do not change them unless necessary. The description for each parameter can be found here.

    You must proceed to the last screen and press Ok or Reboot. If you skip this, the window will appear on every boot.

    To display this window again later, type in the console: GLOBAL

  7. Go to Settings → Firmware Updates

  8. Click Check for Updates, and wait until the check completes

  9. Click Update and update all components.

    If many errors appear — this is normal. Plugins are not part of the firmware and are downloaded separately. Click Check for Updates again, then restore and update each module individually. The printer will reboot during the process.

  10. Enable the recommendations plugin

    Or enter in the console: ENABLE_PLUGIN name=recommend

  11. Send Files via "Octo/Klipper" for Printing

    You need to switch to the Octo/Klipper protocol:

    • Host Type: Octo/Klipper
    • Printer Agent: Moonraker

    For Creator 5 / Creator 5 Pro / AD5X:

    • Hostname: IP_printer

    For FF5M / FF5M Pro:

    • Hostname: IP_printer:7125
    • Device UI: IP_printer or IP_printer:80

  12. Ready-made profiles

    The entire start code should be replaced with this: 

    START_PRINT EXTRUDER_TEMP=[nozzle_temperature_initial_layer] BED_TEMP=[bed_temperature_initial_layer_single]
M190 S[bed_temperature_initial_layer_single]
M104 S[nozzle_temperature_initial_layer] T{single_extruder_multi_material ? 0 : initial_extruder}
SET_PRINT_STATS_INFO TOTAL_LAYER=[total_layer_count]

    START_PRINT EXTRUDER_TEMP=... BED_TEMP=... should be written on one line

    The end code should be this:

    END_PRINT

    Code for before changing the layer to this one:

    SET_PRINT_STATS_INFO CURRENT_LAYER={layer_num + 1}

  13. Enable MD5 verification

  14. Read the recommendations

  15. Read the FAQ
  16. Calibrate the printer
  17. Read the specifics of AD5X and Creator 5 Pro

docs.title: AD5X Warning
docs.text:
@Khamai

After installing the Native Firmware, the print head may not be correctly positioned against the filament receiver (the receiver shutter may not be fully closed, filament may be pushed onto the table, etc.).

Via the engineering menu on the stock firmware

If you encounter this issue, you need to calibrate the print head position using the following algorithm:

  1. Download the Set.XY.Offset.zip archive and unzip it to the root of a flash drive.
  2. Insert the flash drive into the turned-off printer and turn it on.
  3. The calibration interface will appear on the printer screen. Press Reset.
  4. Use the control arrows to position the print head against the receiver so that the print head presses the shutter lever firmly, the nozzle is behind the movable shutter, and the shutter itself is flush with the front surface of the receiver.
  5. Press the Set button to confirm the calibration result.
  6. Remove the flash drive and reboot the printer.

docs.title: Updating the Mod
docs.text:
If the mod displays Update Z-Mod via USB, you must update via USB, even if you updated recently.

Updating via USB preserves all data.

Simplest method: Use the ZFLASH macro. Insert the USB drive, reboot the printer, and run ZFLASH. The macro will:

  • Check for the latest version.
  • Download the latest release for your printer model.
  • Verify checksums.
  • Reboot the printer.
  • Automatically install the update (keep the USB drive inserted for future updates).

After installation:

  1. Go to Fluidd/Mainsail → Settings → Software Update.
  2. Click Check Updates and install the latest Z-Mod updates.

If it shows a lot of errors, that's normal.

Plugins aren't included in the firmware and are downloaded separately.

Click Check for updates. Then restore and update all modules one by one. The printer will reboot during this process.

Version Compatibility:

  • The OS version (under System → Distribution) must match the first two digits of the Z-Mod version (Settings → Updates → Z-Mod).
  • Mismatched versions cause instability.

Manual USB Update:

  1. Format a USB drive to FAT/FAT16/FAT32(MBR).
  2. Copy the mod file to the USB root.
  3. Power off the printer.
  4. Insert the USB drive.
  5. Power on the printer.
  6. Wait for the printer to reboot (do not remove the USB drive).
  7. Wait for the mod installation to complete and for the printer to report success.
  8. Remove the USB drive.
  9. Power cycle the printer.
  10. Go to Fluidd/Mainsail → Settings → Software Update, click Check Updates and install the latest Z-Mod updates.

docs.title: Removing or Temporarily Disabling the Mod
docs.text:
• SKIP_ZMOD: Reboots without starting Moonraker/Fluidd.
  • REMOVE_ZMOD: Fully uninstalls the mod.

Recommended method: Use the REMOVE_ZMOD macro. Use USB removal only if macros are unavailable (after USB removal the Z-Mod boot logo may remain).

Attention!

  • If you are using Klipper 13, you must run UPDATE_MCU. This will prevent the MCU and Klipper from being different versions.
  • If you have enabled plugins, you must first disable them using DISABLE_PLUGIN name=g28_tenz

To remove the mod completely: REMOVE_ZMOD FULL=1

USB Removal:

  1. Format a USB drive to FAT/FAT16/FAT32(MBR).
  2. Copy flashforge_init.sh to the USB root.
  3. Power off the printer.
  4. Insert the USB drive.
  5. Power on the printer.
  6. Wait for three reboots.
  7. Remove the USB drive and use the stock firmware.

docs.title: Updating Stock Firmware
docs.text:
1. Disable all active plugins except recommend, timelapse, and notify: DISABLE_PLUGIN name=plugin_name

  2. If you are using Klipper 13, run UPDATE_MCU before updating the stock firmware. This prevents version mismatch issues between the MCU and Klipper.

  3. Enable Chinese cloud services (if you wish to update via the stock touchscreen): SAVE_ZMOD_DATA CHINA_CLOUD=1

If the native screen does not find updates:

  • Your serial number has not yet been included in the update rollout
  • Install the stock firmware update from a USB drive

For AD5X/Creator 5/Creator 5 Pro, Z-Mod activation from a USB drive after updating the stock firmware:

  • AD5X-enable-zmod.tgz
  • Creator5-enable-zmod.tgz
  • Creator5Pro-enable-zmod.tgz

But if you update from the native screen rather than from a USB drive, run the RESET_PASSWD macro before turning the printer off.

docs.title: Boot Recovery
docs.text:
Guide by @darksimpson, Alexander, @Ikaros413, @SoloMen88

Symptoms: Printer freezes on boot screen and is unreachable via LAN.

Try restoring the firmware by installing a full firmware:

  • FF5M
  • AD5X

Steps:

  1. Unplug the printer.
  2. Prepare a 3.3V UART/USB converter (ensure jumper is set to 3.3V).

  1. Open the printer’s rear panel.
  2. Connect to the UART pins (RX, TX, GND — do NOT connect 3.3V).

WARNING: The converter must be 3.3 V. If you apply 5 V, the CPU will burn out and you will have to replace the motherboard! If your converter has a jumper, MAKE SURE to move it from 5V to 3.3V.

  1. Connect the converter crosswise:

    • Converter RX → Printer TX
    • Converter TX → Printer RX
    • Converter GND → Printer GND

  1. Identify the new COM port in your OS.

  1. Open PuTTY:

    • Connection type: Serial
    • Speed: 115200
    • COM port: (e.g., COM6)

  2. Power on the printer.

  3. When Hit any key to stop autoboot appears, press Enter.

  4. In U-Boot, run: 

    setenv init /bin/sh
boot

  5. After Linux boots, remount the filesystem as writable: 

    mount -t proc proc /proc
mount -o remount,rw /

  6. Fix what is broken, e.g. delete a faulty script, or the camera script if boot fails because of the camera: 

    rm -f /etc/init.d/S01bad_script
rm -f /usr/data/zmod/zmod/.shell/S98camera

  7. Save changes and reboot: 

    sync
reboot
